ety.text: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀧𑀸𑀅 (pāa), from Sanskrit पाद (pā́da) / पद् (pád, “foot”), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *pā́ts, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *pā́ts, and from Proto-Indo-European *pṓds. Compare Persian پا (pâ), Hittite [Term?] (/⁠pata⁠/), Latin pēs, pedis, Tocharian A pe, Tocharian B paiyye, Lithuanian pāda (“sole (foot)”), Russian под (pod, “ground”), Ancient Greek πούς, ποδός (poús, podós), Old Armenian ոտն (otn), English foot. Cognate with Marathi पाय (pāy).

s.g: throwing oneself into or down, falling, fall, downfall

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit पात (pāta). Doublet of वार (vār).

Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *peth₂- Sanskrit पत् (pat) Proto-Indo-European *-tḗr Proto-Indo-European *-trom Sanskrit -त्र (-tra) Sanskrit पत्त्र (pattra) Prakrit 𑀧𑀢𑁆𑀢 (patta) Hindi पात Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit पत्त (patta), from Sanskrit पत्त्र (pattra). Doublet of पत्ता (pattā), पाता (pātā), पत्र (patra), and पत्त्र (pattra). Further related to पत्ती (pattī), पट्ट (paṭṭ), पट्टा (paṭṭā), etc. Related distantly to English feather, petal (through Ancient Greek πέτᾰλον (pétălon, “leaf”)).
